white paper

Source record: docs/studies/analysis/pulsechain_whitepaper_completeness_20261003.md.
Completeness and clarity of the pDAI white paper
3 October 2026. Five fresh-context analysts followed by two shared-draft challenge rounds. Blockchain
work remains read-only.
The paper now states one thesis: distributed wallets could use private-L2 funding, accepted
local issuance and common-unit arbitrage to acquire pDAI and neighboring stables, manage
supply, and fund a separately specified two-sided dollar policy with timely replenishment. It
preserves just-in-time funding without assuming a central treasury or persistent local stockpile.
All five final reviews accepted the revised conditional research account with no blocking corrections. This
agreement establishes review convergence, not proof of private source operation, common control,
available capacity or intended purpose. The maintained white paper (main paper) is the resulting
document.
Four meanings of complete
Question Finding
Does the paper cover the discussed mechanisms? Substantially complete: private L2, exact destination
acceptance, local issuance/conversion, common U,
distributed acquisitions, Curve bases, supply buffers,
native financing, debt/backing, clocks, exits and intent are
present directly or through the retained appendix/studies.
Does it specify a reviewable mechanism? Yes as a conditional architecture, an exact local route
register and a finite research benchmark. Actual source
endpoints, executors, available funding and replenishment
commitments remain unverified deployment fields.
Does it prove a deployed dollar-peg campaign? No. Local components and two profitable closed trades are
demonstrated; the complete fresh-source, repeated-
support and restoration sequence is not.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 458

Question Finding
Does it establish the participants' intent? No. Coordination, accumulation and a dollar objective
remain interpretations that must be compared against
independent arbitrage, monetization and replacement
inflows.
T opic coverage is different from an executable deployment or certainty about intent. A research-selected
test can make the proposition falsifiable without inventing the participants' actual configuration. Optional
issuers, Portal, rebases, native yield and external LPs are alternative capacity branches; universal
governance control is not a necessary premise.
What improved
The original main body was 6,762 words. The revised body is 1,916 words, about 72% shorter; detailed
material remains in the appendix and existing studies. All 43 distinct local study-link targets from the
original paper survive. The initial paper is frozen in the review batch rather than overwriting historical
evidence.
The rewrite organizes the argument around five jobs: source funding, destination acceptance, funded
conversion, price-sensitive trading and replenishment. It distinguishes profitable arbitrage, net
acquisition, common-U relative parity, bounded dollar execution and intent. Each job needs the exact
asset, effective executor, payer, resulting claims and deadline.
Residual buffer language was replaced with collectively executable inputs and permitted just-in-time
delivery. Dollar-reference and restoration decisions were promoted from scattered caveats to explicit
operating requirements. Copied Arbitrum/Optimism gateways, copied Across and the canonical
PulseChain–Ethereum capital boundary are named separately. The core accounting rule remains one
normalized eligible stable unit = U, with token admission, conversion limits and suspension conditions
required.
The appendix adds a minimal direct-delivery/FEI route register. It names existing pDAI, the public FEI
module, existing FEI and its Curve pool, while explicitly leaving the private source and conversion into a
distinct dollar payment token open. A longer receipt/Reserve branch remains a separate construction.
A finite benchmark and its limits
The proposed benchmark uses exactly 1,000 pDAI per request, an all-in 1% band around $1, and a 24-
hour horizon. It predeclares 100 requests on each side in one-sided batches at six-minute intervals.
Refused or expired eligible requests remain in the completion denominator; only counting successful
trades would conceal a funding shortfall.
Quotes record a block, binding acceptance and expiry at b+2. Accepted requests must settle on time;
the independently executable dollar reference is measured at settlement. Quote expiry is not a
guarantee of transaction inclusion. Inputs must arrive before or within execution. Restoring a later quote
cannot repair completed proceeds.
Within an hour after execution, the test requires another 1,000-pDAI order's deliverable capacity on both
sides plus already accepted obligations. Remaining requests need an exact-resource/deadline ledger.
Measuring next-order capacity even after the final request prevents restoration from becoming vacuous.
A 1% payment-reference decline is inside the stated test envelope; larger shocks and greater flows are
not silently advertised as covered.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 459

These are research choices, not deployed contracts or promises attributed to the wallet group. The test
is a specification for historical observation or separately labelled offline economic evaluation; this
investigation did not submit orders or run blockchain execution simulations. Its payment candidate,
actual resources, source obligations and complete service still need evidence.
A focused reference identity checkpoint
The selected payment candidate is PulseChain token 0x15d38573d2feeb82e7ad5187ab8c1d52810b1f07. At chain
369, block 27,699,585, hash 0xd8f0bc5ca2e16f0660c45d5595a6c45712befe5a6de8f8a5830cd9accc433995, getters
confirm:
Name: USD Coin from Ethereum; symbol USDC; six decimals.
T oken implementation: 0x539a69de74e9ed69fbe7f909fa935d05b8caba11.
Owner and bridge contract: 0x4fd0aaa7506f3d9cb8274bdb946ec42a1b8751ef.
Mediator implementation: 0xe64b29deb76616ff5a39e48ea33352dff62a72e4.
Configured foreign token: 0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48.
Configured counterpart: 0x1715a3e4a142d8b698131108995174f37aeba10d.
Copied pUSDC at A0b on PulseChain is a different token from the candidate representation. Chain
identity is essential. Proxy/implementation source responses and verified getter ABI signatures are saved
with the checkpoint. Four successful batches share the same pinned header and each rechecks it.
This establishes local identity, bridge authorization and configured mappings. It does not audit Ethereum
custody, destination claims, actual release, external valuation, pDAI/payment execution, benchmark
capacity, private-L2 connectivity or group control. The raw responses do not substitute for those proofs.
The evidence that would change the conclusion
Three jobs provide more information than additional review agreement:
Exact source/conversion and post-use restoration. Record source rights, fresh authenticated
output, destination acceptance, executor, payer, claims and resulting state. Follow one known local
cycle through an actual refill. Failed acceptance, empty payment resources or missing refill exclude
that route's tested capacity; a view quote or new nominal claim cannot replace the paid asset.
Canonical bridge and distributed acquisition reconstruction. Reconcile per-asset custody,
destination claims, completed deposits/releases, pending obligations and price revaluation. Compare
aggregate purchases, sales, issuance, LP changes and custody without requiring one visible wallet.
Flat marked TVL without replacement quantities weakens the refill interpretation; churn without net
acquisition weakens the accumulation interpretation.
Repeated dollar-responsive support. Observe predeclared eligible requests, all-in outcomes,
funding deadlines and restored capacity under the benchmark's limits. Missed accepted
commitments, out-of-band outcomes, unaccounted obligations or failed refill reject that specified
service. Independent arbitrage can produce support effects; attributing coordination or peg intent
remains a separate question.
One route or benchmark failing does not disprove every possible architecture. One passing episode does
not establish perpetual support. Those boundaries keep the next work informative rather than turning
every outcome into confirmation.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 460

Method and reproduction
The roles were mechanism, evidence, completeness, economics and clarity. Round 1 used fresh contexts
and the frozen paper without peer reports. Rounds 2 and 3 challenged shared revised papers and
preceding assessments. Fifteen individual Markdown/JSON reports are preserved. No actual human
comprehension test or calibrated probability was claimed.
The explicit experiment is Research/experiments/pulsechain_whitepaper_completeness_20261003.json. Frozen
papers, the 71-study initial index, assessments, source responses and checkpoint are in ignored 
artifacts/pulsechain-whitepaper-completeness-20261003/. Read-only reference probes have explicit getter
manifests named pulsechain_dollar_reference_token_20261003.json, 
pulsechain_dollar_reference_identity_20261003.json, pulsechain_dollar_reference_mediator_20261003.json and 
pulsechain_dollar_reference_mapping_20261003.json under Research/experiments/.
Reproduction checks validate frozen hashes, report schemas, getter ABI/view signatures, pinned
headers, decoded identities, study-link preservation and saved documents. All prior archive, recovery
and historical research identities remain unchanged. Application code was not modified.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 461
